newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares sink at noon on pessimism.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares sink at noon on pessimism.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market fell sharply at midday on Wednesday, with short-term pessimism growing in the light of the market's recent prevailing bearishness, brokers said.
The B share index dipped 4.10 points or 2.79 percent to 142.84 on turnover of HK$37 million.
The domestic A share index inched up 0.41 points or 0.09 percent to 464.00 on turnover of 4.8 billion yuan.
"The B share market's recent poor performance ddnted investor confidence," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Buying interest has been evaporating, with investorspartictlarly selling Shenzhen-based B share companies," the analyst said.
Shenzhen-based Chiwal Petroleum Base was the biggest loser, tumbming HK$0.24 or 8.79 percent to HK$2.80.
Some local B share issues fared better on speculation that Hong Kong's reversion to China would boost neighbouring Shenzhen's economy, brokers said.
But buying interest in local shares has begun to decline with the handover just several days away, they said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese control at midnight on June 30.
Chiwan Wharf, which handles port facilities in Shenzhen, was the second worst performer, dropping HK$0.40 or 8.11 percent to HK$4.53.
On the A share market, recently-listed First Automobile rose 0.09 yuan to 14.70 yuan on volume of 73 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.
Brokers said the A share market gains were capped by concerns that Beijing may carry out some new anti-speculation measures after July 1.
